newsitem.title: USA: Inglewood, Calif. drops arena deal after Prop. 218.
newsitem.headline: Inglewood, Calif. drops arena deal after Prop. 218.

text.p: Inglewood, Calif., was forced to pull its offer to help finance a sports arena following passage of Proposition 218, which cast doubt on three taxes approved by the city, officials said Friday.

In September, the Inglewood city council passed hotel, parking lot and ticket tax increases to help developers build a proposed $200 million arena. The funds would have been used in part to secure bonds to raise $35 million for the arena.
"We withdrew our current offer on the table partly because of Prop. 218, but it's also because we're taking a look at the overall offer," Assistant City Manager Norman Cravens said.

Inglewood made the financial offer in a bid to keep the Lakers basketball team and Kings hockey team in the city. Inglewood's Proposition 218 setback was expected to boost the bid by Los Angeles to attract the teams.
Cravens said Inglewood expects to unveil a new plan to help finance an arena proposal within the next week.
Proposition 218, which was approved by voters this week, requires that local taxes be submitted to voters for approval.
